gen-mystery-quest-gf-suwannaphum: Suwannaphum reads dignified and editorial, its text serif letters tall and wide-mouthed, almost like squared-off woodblock type. And Mystery Quest, bookish and nostalgic, tucks compact ascenders above its lowercase, giving headings an old-print feel.
gen-nixie-one-gf-bhutuka-expanded-one: Retro-tech lettering, then a literary voice. Nixie One keeps a constant stroke from top to baseline, while BhuTuka Expanded One, a text serif with curvy, unclamped letters, slows reading to a leisurely walk.
gen-nixie-one-gf-hepta-slab: Nostalgic, retro-tech Nixie One draws open curves with clear gaps, one stroke running top to baseline. Hepta Slab, a text serif, lets stretched-out words breathe with open counters, adding a bookish, dignified footing underneath the heading.
gen-gf-oxanium-poppins: Poppins is modern and clean, with sturdy tall lowercase and loose curves that sit quietly beneath the commanding Oxanium. Long paragraphs would flow without any thick-thin flicker snagging the eye.
gen-eater-fs-epilogue: Eater is dark and aggressive, with wide gaps between its letters. Epilogue, approachable and contemporary, would carry paragraphs easily, its curvy monoline letters staying relaxed from line to line.
gen-flavors-fs-asap: A towering x-height, like a stubby carpenter's pencil stroke, gives Flavors its whimsical, commanding look. Asap follows with open-arced c forms and a body height close to the capitals, keeping things readable.
gen-gf-autour-one-fs-epilogue: A clear channel leads into every round letter of Autour One, so its bold, expressive shapes never clog. Epilogue does the quieter work, with a wire-like monoline skeleton and a tall body that stays approachable.
gen-megrim-gf-lexend-tera: Megrim is angular and futuristic, all skyward x-height and measured stroke ends. Lexend Tera does the steadier job, a plotter-pen line of open-faced curves with letters spaced like stepping stones.
gen-mystery-quest-instrument-sans: Instrument Sans has c ends pointing apart like open pincers and a stroke weight that never varies, clean and modern. Mystery Quest supplies the bookish, nostalgic voice up top, with compact ascenders.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-lexend-mega: Cheerful and loud, Luckiest Guy pours its ink at one width, with a high mean line. And Lexend Mega, approachable and modern, is best kept at a modest size, its c ends staying visibly apart.
